passage.title: Teacher-written memoir extract for the Year 9 end-of-year test (TGA)
paras: My first editor gave me one rule: write what you see, not what you are told to see. It sounded simple. It was not. On my first big story, a factory fire, the owner's spokesman met me at the gate with a printed statement. Everything was under control, it said; no one was at risk. Behind him, I could see the night shift standing in the car park in their socks. I wrote down the statement. Then I wrote down the socks. The next morning, the socks were the story. I have kept that notebook for thirty years, and I still open it when I am tempted to take the easy version of the truth.

head: Q
Task
Marks
rows: Give two details about the fire that the statement left out
How does the writer use language to show the difference between the statement and the truth?
How is the text structured to build towards its message?
'The writer suggests that truth is found in small details.' How far do you agree?
